Salla Cenág (I29)

Region in the English ranking survey: Escann.

In one sentence: Carry the wounds of your family out of the Deepwoods, choose between vengeance and tolerance, and turn an isolated Wood Elf clan into pathfinders towards the wider world.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 68/100 | Authoritarianism 48/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 86/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 68/100) | Pluralism 70/100.

v2.1 values: Neutral (65/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (29 unique missions, plus shared Wood Elf missions) | Mission-tree update context: local Mod v1.37.5.0; a 2025 official diary introduced the rework | Uniqueness: High | Waiting and grind: Medium | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion capacity: Medium-high.

Kinship and Old Wounds in the Bone Grove

Salla Cenág is a Wood Elf tribe in the Deepwoods in 1444, following the Fey Court and organised under a clan government. Alara leads the clan, with Lanhara of Salla Ayeth as her consort. Starting history also establishes the Verdant Pact and friendships with other Wood Elf clans. This is neither an already established branch of an elven empire nor merely a small country with forest defence bonuses: the relationship between the clan leader and her kin directly shapes the national story. [Local history script; Chinese localisation]

The offline English Wiki places Salla Cenág in the distinctive environment of the Bone Grove. The clan is small and relatively isolated, yet places extraordinary importance on an extended understanding of family. The accumulated bones have also encouraged a bleak understanding of the struggle between life and death. Intimacy does not mean equality: the Wiki records internal punishments that can include forced labour and exile. This background explains both their loyalty in protecting companions and their capacity to hold long grudges against those who injure their kin. [Wiki lore]

In 1428, an elven apprentice died while investigating the Verdant Veil, drawing Cenág and Drennen into the Cousins' War; intervention by goblin warlocks deepened the hatred. Alara faces more than a simple story of invaders and reconquest: misunderstandings between elves, bereavement and third-party powers within the forest are entangled. The Wiki also describes renewed orc pressure prompting an alliance in 1441, while local history already sets clan friendships and the Pact in 1430. These chronological layers do not agree and cannot be merged into an uncontested timeline. The player's starting relationships follow the local script. [Wiki lore; local history script]

Vengeance Is Not the Only Way

The main route combines 29 Cenág-specific missions with 13 shared Wood Elf missions. The structured query also includes 2 generic missions, so all 44 must not be described as unique national missions. The dedicated story concerns reunited kin, old grudges against goblins, the war against Sapchopper and leaving the forest. [Local script]

The fate of the Bone Grove goblins has explicit branches: tolerant, intolerant and undecided states alter later conditions and rewards. The country is not predetermined from the start to be either "friendly elves" or "exterminating avengers". The tolerant route asks Alara to recognise that aid, sacrifice and past injury can coexist; the hard-line route lets an unforgettable bereavement continue to govern policy. Personality and value assessments must preserve the choice rather than assign one route's actions to every player. [Local script; local narrative text]

The kinship storyline requires repairing ties between Cenág, Drennen and Ayeth. Marriage and family bonds are not decoration: they connect diplomacy, integration and character stories. The Sapchopper route also requires intelligence networks and military advantage; if the opponent has already disappeared, the mission provides corresponding alternative handling. Defeating the enemy is not enough—you must give your own clan alliance a durable footing. [Local script; local narrative text]

From the Forest Exit to the World

Exploration is the country's most distinctive development direction. Its missions encourage discovering the outside world, establishing a city towards Daravan's Folly, acquiring a harbour and encountering Ourdia, Bahar and more distant peoples. Expansion means more than painting the map: it lets Wood Elves long separated by the forest and Veil rediscover the world. Those external connections also challenge their existing clan identity. [Local script; local narrative text]

In practice, secure the forest wars, decide Bone Grove policy and maintain kinship ties first. In the middle game, open the forest exit and connect colonisation, a harbour and external diplomacy. Later, address clan unification and broader political relationships. Eligible Wood Elf countries can form Cyranvar (I45), but the decision changes Tag and reallocates non-generic missions; the Cenág-specific tree cannot be described as unconditionally preserved intact in the new country. Character survival, branch decisions and cooperation with other countries affect the pacing. These are conditional player futures, not a history the Wiki has already chosen for the player.

Personality and Player Choice

The provisional coordinates are Expansion 68 / Authoritarianism 48 / Magic–Artifice direction 86 (intensity 68) / Pluralism 70. The overall value assessment is Neutral 65 and mainly depends on the branch. Protecting kin, repairing the community and conditional acceptance of outsiders provide positive grounds; harsh internal punishments, vengeance and exclusion limit a higher assessment. Elven identity, war or cultural unification does not itself change the moral score, and goblins are assessed as fully sapient persons. [Local narrative text; Wiki lore]

The official Deepwoods diary presents Cenág as explorers and emphasises Alara's assumption of leadership after personal tragedy. Some content was still in development when the diary appeared, so it does not certify every current detail. Player discussions focus on ruler survival, clan unification and cooperation with Ourdia. One post has conflicting date metadata and is retained only as an experience with an uncertain version context. [Official developer diary; community opinion]

Recommended for players who enjoy character relationships, exploration, diplomacy and social-policy choices. If you only want straightforward conquest without diplomatic preparation, this country is not the easiest fit. See the original research evidence for formation and branch boundaries, and the English source receipt for this translation's checks.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when that set is adopted; seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Only national ideas themselves are listed: racial, government and mission rewards are not mixed into their numbers, and a successor's new ideas do not automatically stack with the old ones. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals; they do not automatically describe events already completed in 1444.

Descriptions use native English originals rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Numerical displays are inherited from the Chinese research data; where the display unit is uncertain it is explicitly qualified, not silently corrected. The seven alternative Cyranvar sets below retain their actual script conditions and are not seven sets simultaneously granted to Cenág.

Salla Cenág (I29) — Salla Cenág Ideas

Traditions: Cenága Traditions

Effects: Movement Speed: +15%; shock_damage_received：-10%.

Idea 1: The Bone Struggle

Whilst living in the morbid environment of the Bone Grove for a millennium, the elves of Salla Cenág view and concept of death has grown into a philosophy known as Yfel Cenág or "the Bone Struggle”.

For the clan, Life is a constant struggle to stave off Death, one that no elf nor idea is immune to. Indeed, all that separates Life from Death is motion and the desire to continue. That which remains still has given into the Death. Faced with this, the tides of change are not meant to be feared but riden.

Effects: Idea Cost: -10%.

Idea 2: Horrors of the Bone Grove

Bones of animals, of enemies, and of friends litter the Bone Grove. It is even well known that bones older than the elven presence in the forest can be found. Lesser known to outsiders are the horrifying monsters that stalk within its twisting passages. The most dreaded of these feytouched beings are known as the Bone Hoarders, who strain the mortal mind with their grim promises of death delivered through grisly visions. They are avoided at all costs by the grove inhabitants, and are the subject of terrified whispers of both children and elders alike.

Such are the harsh conditions for those who eek out within the Bone Grove. Those who survive are are stronger for it. Those who cannot... end up as the freshest set of bones to decorate the grove.

Effects: Attrition for Enemies: +100%; Supply Limit Modifier: +15%.

Idea 3: Bound by Blood

Salla Cenág’s roots are as scouts, sent to explore the Bone Grove and track the movement of the various goblin clans in the area. Even their earliest encampments were built later than most of the other elven clans due to the harsh environment of the Bone Grove. Within the terrifying and dangerous environments of the grove, surrounded by goblins, and lost in the confusing fey-touched landscape, clan cohesion proved vital for survival. When desperately struggling for every inch of territory, even a single elf turned traitor could potentially spell doom for all. As a consequence, a culture of tightly knit groups began to take root.

In the modern day, there is no higher priority to the elves of Salla Cenág than one’s family. The concept of family is also much larger than in many other societies – the family includes not just the immediate relatives, but anyone that shares blood. Crimes committed against your own kin is taboo, met with punishments many outsiders decry as draconian, and yet, the culture persists, producing a society that fights for and with each other.

Effects: Yearly Corruption: -0.1.

Idea 4: Bonecoated Infiltrators

For centuries, hunters within the Bone Grove used a special mix of crushed feytouched bone dust to help them with their hunts. This mixture reduced their presence by giving them a natural camouflage, which meshed well with their scouting heritage. Whilst this technique was applied to hunting for generations, its potential for warfare began to shine during the rise of Oubblig and his goblins and later the orcs of the Greentide.

It was during this new age of war that the combined efforts of Ceanna Alara Cenág and her beloved Lanhara Ayeth’s changes to the military began. Perhaps the biggest change was the creation of the Bonecoated Infiltrators, an elite force of elves dusted in the traditional hunting mix with the goal to find and infiltrate enemy encampments and cause mayhem from the inside. This style of guerilla warfare in conjunction with traditional assaults by the rest of the Cenága’s forces would find its brightest moments following the creation of the Verdant Pact.

Effects: Siege Ability: +10%.

Idea 5: Thyr Agoriad

One thousand years… for one thousand years the elves of the Deepwoods struggled in isolation within a feytouched pocket dimension, entrapped by the Verdant Veil. In this time, countless attempts at escape were tried. All failed. Indeed, escape may have been impossible were it not for a fateful encounter with Corin, the Avatar of Agrados. And in her wake came Thyr Agoriad, the Opening.

Lasting from 1443 to the early 1500s, the Opening brought upon countless changes to the remaining Wood Elven clans. From new ways of fighting in the form of Diranbe glaivedancing to the codification of Deepwoods Druidism through Magisterium’s Schools of Magic to simple access to the latest form of the wheeled plow, the period was nothing short of a cultural renaissance. One that may have gone on decades longer were it not for the rise of the Emeraldtide…

Effects: Goods Produced Modifier: +5%; Global Institution Spread: +20%.

Idea 6: Heralds of a New Age

Every era has its heroes. Names who history remembers met the challenges of their time. Yet, no other time in Wood Elven history can compare to the sheer number to rise during the 15th and 16th centuries - silver tongued Narawen Drennen, ruthless Oberon Fealgarn, bold Alara Cenag, cunning Selussa Ghul, relentless Elaria Ayeth, fearless Faevir Vaytcothyd. It is their legacy that ensured a new age for Wood Elvenkind.

Effects: Leader Cost: -10%.

Idea 7: The Oak Oath

The Verdant Pact was the first step to transforming the clans into one state. Yet, by itself, the journey may have ended there; for while defending another clan may have been acceptable, ceding independence to another was not.

Only after the ruinous Emeraldtide, which saw destruction of one clan, the wholesale displacement of another and near wholesale enslavement to the Blackened Prince and his minions, did this attitude change. Having faced true existential destruction, the remaining surviving clans solemnly agreed to gather before the venerable oak where the mother of Wood Elvenkind, Commander Liandel Speardancer was laid to rest. There, for the first time in over a millennium, they elected a new Commander, a Cennasai, to lead the elves of the Deepwoods forward as one state: Cyranvar.

Effects: Liberty Desire in Subjects: +1000% (inherited display; unit conversion unverified); Diplomatic Annexation Cost: -10%.

Traditions: Cyranvari Traditions

Effects: Attrition for Enemies: +100%; Movement Speed: +20%.

Idea 1: The Grand Opening

Our time in isolation has seen the world change drastically from when our ancestors first entered the shadowed boughs of the Deepwoods. Though we have managed to set aside our petty squabbles and unite, we find ourselves still under threat. We shall open the Deepwoods to the peoples of Cannor so that we might learn from their wisdom lest we stay stuck in our backwards ways and find ourselves threatened beyond our ability to defend.

Effects: Global Institution Spread: +25%.

Idea 2: The Green Palace

We have always been a divided people, more prone to tribal or familial loyalties than to any sense of national identity. The invasion of the Deepwoods by the orcish brutes changed that. Our division allowed them to run rampant, ruining the equilibrium of our home and threatening our relationship with the Fey. Now that we have driven out these beasts, and the Verdant Pact has coalesced into a true union of the tribes, we must build a palace truly befitting the High King of the Deepwoods.

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican Tradition: +0.3; Horde Unity: +1.

Idea 3: One People, One Country

The Greentide beset upon us with a ferocious savagery and those tribes who were too stubborn to join the Verdant Pact found themselves annihilated. Now that the wars have ceased and our homeland is no longer under threat, there are some who mutter about a desire to return to the old ways. However, most have come to see the value of solidarity and realize that the Deepwoods cannot insulate us from the world as it has done in the past. We must become as one people, all willing to sacrifice for our adopted home lest the tides of change sweep us away.

Effects: Stability Cost Modifier: -15%.

Idea 4: Between Branches and Leaves

Even in times of peace our people inadvertently prepare for war, for use of the longbow is as much a matter of daily survival as it is for battle. Even the least skilled among us are capable to wielding our ancestral weapon to deadly effect. In times past we would answer the calls of the so often capricious fey and ride to war for some elusive ends. Many of the peoples who borders the Deepwoods still have folk stories warning children that if they misbehave then the fey-folk will steal them away in their sleep. Though it has been centuries, the Escanni saying that it is easier to shoot an arrow through branches and leaves than it is to please the Gods hearkens back to a time when such raids were common. The precision of our ancestors skill continues on to this day.

Effects: Land Fire Damage: +15%.

Idea 5: The Oak Gift

Although the Deepwoods and the fey who inhabit them appear fickle by nature, our ancestors were able to see the pattern of balance underlying all things. From this came our role as stewards and servants of this misunderstood land. Though the woods are just as likely to be bereft of bounty we know that this simply hearkens to a time to come when such things will overflow. Our ability to identify this natural cycle ensures that we never want for goods that we need because we strive to never disrupt the equilibrium of the woods.

Effects: Goods Produced Modifier: +10%; National Supply Limit Modifier: +25%.

Idea 6: The Eyes of the Forest

Though many of our kind have left the safety and comfort of the Deepwoods since their opening hoping to find a better life across Cannor, many of them are actually Eyes of the Forest, sent forth by the High King at the bidding of the fey. They aim to understand the world around us and ensure that a threat like the Greentide is never able to catch our peoples unaware again. The fact that many peoples have an attitude of ingrained dismissiveness towards our kind only makes this task easier; no suspects that beneath the downtrodden visage of a sapling lies the hardened mind of an Eye.

Effects: Spy Network Construction: +20%; global_spy_defence：+20%.

Idea 7: A Bow in every Home

During the orcish onslaught, our people quickly learned that just as the darkened woodscape veiled us from the world, so too for the greenskins as well. Battles were often swift and brutal and those found unprepared were slaughtered by the invaders. This lesson taught that laxity rests as the worst of sins, for only through preparedness were we able to throw back the orcish tide and save our precious homeland. Should any other threat arise either within or beyond our borders they will find that the once disparate people of Deepwoods are prepared to sacrifice their lives to defend their homeland.

Effects: Infantry Fire: +15%.

Ambition: Cyranvari Ambition

Effects: Domestic Trade Power: +20%.

Traditions: Cyranvari Traditions

Effects: Vassal Income: +33%; Special Unit Force Limit: +10%.

Idea 1: Gather the Conclave

For the Chroniclers in Anbenncóst it is easy to “The unification of elven clans began at the Conclave of Elynaile.” I admit, even in my foolish youth, as I fought with glaive and bow against the invaders, I could feel something changing. All of us could. But, I promise you, we were not one people back then. If we were, then why were there more conclaves?

Trust took time to build. But as Cinrthir later Farwen Elyn gathered the clans time and again to reclaim each grove, I felt myself ever closer to my fellow elf. Knowing we fought for a shared cause of all our choosing bound us tighter than any authority could.

I could not say which conclave was the one that forever tied the clans together. And I promise you no chronicler could either. What I can say is that even today, more than a century after my last soldiering days, those ties still hold. And that they grow ever stronger with each conclave the Ceannasai calls.

Effects: Vassal Force Limit Contribution: +100%.

Idea 2: The Oak Oath

It’s funny to me, the things we remember. I couldn’t tell you who I stood by the day we took the first Oak Oath. I don’t remember what I wore or even the day it happened. What I do remember is what my heart felt. Awe, watching the ceanns and ceannas, each heroes of the Greentide in their own right, kneeled before the Ceannasai. Pride, as the Ceannasai, our commander, called us together as one people divided no longer. Resolve, as I and a hundred, no, a thousand others recited the Oath. Ahh, when I close my eyes, I can still hear their voices and my own as one uttering those solemn words:

On the name of my forebears I pledge myself to my fellow elf Blood or no, we are forever kin I pledge to heed without question The word of my Commander Voice and protector of my kin I pledge to forever stand true As the Oak through the turning of season

Effects: Ruler Culture Advisor Cost: -10%; All Estates Loyalty Equilibrium: +5%.

Idea 3: Bond of Silver

Even when I was a Bloomer, barely half a century to my name serving my last years as a ranger, I could not help but notice how the memory of the Veil was quickly fading. Those who were born after did not understand the isolation we older elves had resigned ourselves to. Back then, the woods were wilder. Travel beyond one's grove was a rarity. It was quite the event to just see your cousins in another grove.\N\NAye, I suppose such a time would be impossible to imagine now. With the Veil gone, and especially after the Moon Elves of the Redglades stumbled upon us, the world has opened into a vast expanse. Elves and even humans travel freely hailing Lorent, Anbennar, Celmaldor and beyond. All names that still twist my tongue.

Effects: Improve Relations: +15%; Diplomatic Relations: +2.

Idea 4: Thyr Athraythe

The Elders always spoke so highly of the past. I, like so many younger elves, often had to hide my scoffs and eye rolls as they waxed and waned about how the previous century had been so much better. Yet now that I have seen nearly two hundred years myself, I can’t help but curse the folly of youth.

The history books call it the Rebirth, Tyr Athraythe in our own tongue. For me, though, it was simply a happier time. After spending my years as a Sapling at war, I found a life beyond it - potion making. Indeed so too did many of my kin find joy in peace. Neighboring my shop were stores offering all sorts of goods once restricted to the grove they came from. Wine from the Lake Grove, ivory carvings from the Bone Grove, spices and herbs (perfect for potions) from the Flower Grove. Indeed, in exchange for my rather excellent potions, I found myself never enough bottles of fine Chilac wine, too many racks full of reagents, and, eventually, something priceless - love.

Effects: Goods Produced Modifier: +15%.

Idea 5: At the Center of Three Worlds

The thing about outsiders is how they always gawk when they come to our lands. I don’t blame them, I suppose. Turns out our sort of normal isn’t like theirs. Your average Moon Elf can’t take a bite of (much less appreciate) boiled bark. For all their bluster, dwarves aren’t used to screaming at the local boggles for tearing up the field. And good luck finding a human who can handle a satyr.

Of course that goes both ways. As my little shop grew into something bigger, I met all sorts of strange folk I learned to call friends. Lyra of Turnmarket, a Corinite Greave from Stalbor was an excellent customer who never ceased to tell tales of crimson rain and Corin’s cause. Madarûn Ironbeard, a dwarf “merchant” (I always suspected a smuggler, but ignorance is a valuable thing) who always seemed to be both on the in and out of every cartel in the Serpentspine. And, of course, Jaddarésa Bedavírar, a harpy named after the daughter of the fabled first Herald of the Jadd Empire. A fact she insisted on telling me and every customer. Seelie Queen smile upon her, in all my years, never have I met someone as sweet and dogged as her. Forty years and she still tries to bring the light of the Jadd to my life.

Effects: Domestic Trade Power: +20%.

Idea 6: Ash Children

By the time those feyscorned guns made their way to Cyranvar, my days as a soldier were long behind me. The same could not be said for my wayward daughter. When I look back, I feel pride. Her skill as a sharpshooter easily outclassed my own and her sense of duty toward our people mirrored my own when the forest was still divided between the clans. But at the time, I could only shake my head in disapproval. She and her cohort acted like any sapling would, rebellious and brash. They needed a stern hand to correct this.

To my then bafflement, the Ceannacai encouraged this new generation’s behavior. Dubbing them Ash Children, they were marched to battle equipped with those ructious weapons. Gone were the simple days of the bow and glaive. It was a new era, one filled with bellowing smoke, manic war cries, and neverending cacophony of fire.

Effects: Infantry Fire: +15%.

Idea 7: The War of the Black Tower

Something said can never be unsaid. And after words not worth repeating, my daughter left my shop. Fury gripped me at first, but when she did not return, anger chilled to sorrow. I could not find her, and so I gave myself to my work. Built a mercantile empire dedicated to tracking my lost scion. I did not care when the War of Treachery began. I paid no heed as Esthil and its Witch-Queen lich rose the dead to fight their perverse war.

Even as the old elven clans who had settled Escann warned of the growing threat, not a word could reach my ears. It was only when a young man carrying a shattered sword showed up to my step was I shaken from stupor. At my first sight, and to my shame, all I saw was the union of an elf… and an orc. It was only when I locked eyes with him did I see him for who he was, not simply what.

He was Elrac of Dustandar, proud member of Arturos’ Watch. And he was my grandson.

I cannot begin to express my regrets here. Nor is there time. Elrac, just as his mother, and perhaps just as this old elf was, is driven by sworn duty. No… I remember my oath well. Evil is ascendent and my kin are in need. I will organize an audience for Elrac with the Ceannacai. Cyranvar and its commander must act.

Effects: Army Tradition: +1; Diplomatic Reputation: +100% (inherited display; percentage conversion unverified).

Ambition: Cyranvari Ambition

Effects: Primary Culture Development Cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Face the Axe

Anyone who hasn’t felt the fear of battle’s eve is either a fool or a dead elf walking in my eyes. Once you behold the sight of an orcish host, hear the howls of their warcries, feel the tension of simply waiting for the blood to spill - it gnaws at the spirit. The fear becomes heavy, a weight that threatens to break you before the first arrow has been loosed.

I’m certain when Narawen Drennen turned to address us, she felt it too. How else could the then Ceanna of Salla Drennen have spoken with such conviction? Even now, a century later and her words still ring in my ears.

“Turn not from the foe, for the foe you cannot see will strike you dead. Turn not from your fear, for the fear you do not know will beat you broken. Face your foe, face your fear. Face the axe.“

Effects: morale_damage_received：-10%.

Idea 3: How It's Done

I am no druid. As the Cannorians say, I lack “the spark” of magic. However, that doesn’t mean I am ignorant of it or the bounties it’s given the elves of Cyranvar.

It was magic that renewed the Veil and smoothed the tear between our realm and the fey’s. It was magic that brought the verdant blooms of plants and crops. It was magic that began the end of the wars. After all, it was no blade that killed Khagur Sapchopper - but a bolt of lightning.

Effects: All Power Costs: -2.5%.

Idea 7: The War of the Black Tower

Something said can never be unsaid. And after words not worth repeating, my daughter left my shop. Fury gripped me at first, but when she did not return, anger chilled to sorrow. I could not find her, and so I gave myself to my work. Built a mercantile empire dedicated to tracking my lost scion. I did not care when the War of Treachery began. I paid no heed as Esthil and its Witch-Queen lich rose the dead to fight their perverse war.

Even as the old elven clans who had settled Escann warned of the growing threat, not a word could reach my ears. It was only when a young man carrying a shattered sword showed up to my step was I shaken from stupor. At my first sight, and to my shame, all I saw was the union of an elf… and an orc. It was only when I locked eyes with him did I see him for who he was, not simply what.

He was Elrac of Dustandar, proud member of Arturos’ Watch. And he was my grandson.

I cannot begin to express my regrets here. Nor is there time. Elrac, just as his mother, and perhaps just as this old elf was, is driven by sworn duty. No… I remember my oath well. Evil is ascendent and my kin are in need. I will organize an audience for Elrac with the Ceannacai. Cyranvar and its commander must act.

Idea 1: Cenaga Vanguards

Did I expect the clans to unite under Salla Cenág? Honestly, not at first. Certainly not after the Conclave. Sure, my fellow rangers and myself knew something had changed when we first heard of the Verdant Pact, but back then we were all just focused on just surviving.

So when did I begin to realize what the future heralded? It wasn’t when Clan Sapchopper was felled. Or when I learned of the distant expeditions led by Cenaga elves to fetid swamps and beyond. Nor was it when Ayeth and Drennen bound themselves to Cenag.

Doubt me if you wish, but it was before all that. The moment struck me when I found myself no longer simply thrashing through the wilds of the Deepwoods, but marching through freshly cut paths following subtly etched signs of where to strike and when. Standing there in the depths of the forest, I realized it was the elves of the Bone Grove who were leading me and my rangers to victory… and the future.

Effects: Movement Speed: +20%; Morale Damage: +10%.

Idea 2: The Oak Oath

It’s funny to me, the things we remember. I couldn’t tell you who I stood by the day we took the first Oak Oath. I don’t remember what I wore or even the day it happened. What I do remember is what my heart felt. Awe, watching the ceanns and ceannas, each heroes of the Greentide in their own right, kneeled before the Ceannasai. Pride, as the Ceannasai, our commander, called us together as one people divided no longer. Resolve, as I and a hundred, no, a thousand others recited the Oath. Ahh, when I close my eyes, I can still hear their voices and my own as one uttering those solemn words:

On the name of my forebears I pledge myself to my fellow elf Blood or no, we are forever kin I pledge to heed without question The word of my Commander Voice and protector of my kin I pledge to forever stand true As the Oak through the turning of season

Effects: Ruler Culture Advisor Cost: -10%; All Estates Loyalty Equilibrium: +5%.

Idea 3: New Leaves

For all the years I spent fighting, I’ll be the first to admit I was never an exceptional ranger. Outside of a few fleeting glimpses, the true heroes of the woods were always beyond me. The ceanns, ceannas, and later the Ceannacai were always elves to be admired from afar amongst the rank and file. While my later years would change this, I could not understate my surprise when the first Ceannacai chose to sit at my table one evening.

It shames me to admit the dulling of time, and too many drinks of the moment, has left my recollection lacking. However, even after a century, I can still see the jubilant smile of Cyranvar’s first commander. I can hear their boisterous laughs. And, I can still feel echoes of their words. “The elves of my home clan believe life is a struggle. That only change can stave off death. I realize now there is more to it. Leaves change, yet they too must wilt, fall, and fade. But… that is not the end. As the old turns to soil, new leaves grow anew.”

Effects: Reform Progress Growth: +15%.

Idea 4: Thyr Athraythe

The Elders always spoke so highly of the past. I, like so many younger elves, often had to hide my scoffs and eye rolls as they waxed and waned about how the previous century had been so much better. Yet now that I have seen nearly two hundred years myself, I can’t help but curse the folly of youth.

The history books call it the Rebirth, Tyr Athraythe in our own tongue. For me, though, it was simply a happier time. After spending my years as a Sapling at war, I found a life beyond it - potion making. Indeed so too did many of my kin find joy in peace. Neighboring my shop were stores offering all sorts of goods once restricted to the grove they came from. Wine from the Lake Grove, ivory carvings from the Bone Grove, spices and herbs (perfect for potions) from the Flower Grove. Indeed, in exchange for my rather excellent potions, I found myself never enough bottles of fine Chilac wine, too many racks full of reagents, and, eventually, something priceless - love.

Effects: Goods Produced Modifier: +15%.

Idea 5: At the Center of Three Worlds

The thing about outsiders is how they always gawk when they come to our lands. I don’t blame them, I suppose. Turns out our sort of normal isn’t like theirs. Your average Moon Elf can’t take a bite of (much less appreciate) boiled bark. For all their bluster, dwarves aren’t used to screaming at the local boggles for tearing up the field. And good luck finding a human who can handle a satyr.

Of course that goes both ways. As my little shop grew into something bigger, I met all sorts of strange folk I learned to call friends. Lyra of Turnmarket, a Corinite Greave from Stalbor was an excellent customer who never ceased to tell tales of crimson rain and Corin’s cause. Madarûn Ironbeard, a dwarf “merchant” (I always suspected a smuggler, but ignorance is a valuable thing) who always seemed to be both on the in and out of every cartel in the Serpentspine. And, of course, Jaddarésa Bedavírar, a harpy named after the daughter of the fabled first Herald of the Jadd Empire. A fact she insisted on telling me and every customer. Seelie Queen smile upon her, in all my years, never have I met someone as sweet and dogged as her. Forty years and she still tries to bring the light of the Jadd to my life.

Effects: Domestic Trade Power: +20%.

Idea 6: Ash Children

By the time those feyscorned guns made their way to Cyranvar, my days as a soldier were long behind me. The same could not be said for my wayward daughter. When I look back, I feel pride. Her skill as a sharpshooter easily outclassed my own and her sense of duty toward our people mirrored my own when the forest was still divided between the clans. But at the time, I could only shake my head in disapproval. She and her cohort acted like any sapling would, rebellious and brash. They needed a stern hand to correct this.

To my then bafflement, the Ceannacai encouraged this new generation’s behavior. Dubbing them Ash Children, they were marched to battle equipped with those ructious weapons. Gone were the simple days of the bow and glaive. It was a new era, one filled with bellowing smoke, manic war cries, and neverending cacophony of fire.

Idea 1: Face the Arrow

When it comes to spilling blood, no one ever comes out clean. Anyone fighting a war is quick to learn that lesson. What I didn’t realize was how much worse it could get. It wasn’t until my fellow rangers and I fell under Elaria Ayeth’s command that I learned how far the depravities of war go.

Blind all but one survivor so that they may lead their maimed comrades back to their chieftain. Burn the foe’s fields but not their homes so that they may know the dying pain of starvation. Strike at all times so that they may never know respite, so that they fear even the shadows and sway of the leaves. Break their spirits so they pray to whatever power they wish for escape. Then… teach them the final lesson. “There is no escape in the end, all must Face the Arrow.”

That is all I have to say of that. I wish to consider those times no more.

Effects: Recruitable Ranger Regiment Percentage: +100%; Harsh Treatment Cost: -25%.

Idea 3: Artisians of Living Wood

I have no doubt that the Prince of Fools takes much merriment in one the greatest ironies of these woods - the elves of Ayeth, the greatest archers of the clans, were also peerless in woodcraft. How they balanced the pursuit of martial prowess and masterful craftsmanship remains a mystery to me, but their legacy in Cyranvar is undeniable. From Hall of Heroes in Ciranmyna, resculpted out living Córyn trees taken from the Arrow Grove, to the Elynaile’s Everglow Halls, made abright by the careful coaxing of vayt-bulbs plucked and grafted onto the wooden walls, their works enrich all of the clans and Cyranvar itself.

Idea 1: Auralarn Academy

There is no shortage of tales to bring wonderment, and slumber, to a fussy child. Silly stories of satyrs frolicking the River Grove. Fables full of fairies helping lost wanders. My daughter’s favorites were always those of the huntsmen and huntresses of Auralarn Academy. I must profess to have agreed with her taste, for what story is more riveting than those you witnessed for yourself and still cannot believe?

Imagine the threat of the Greentide and promise of the Verdant Pact being swallowed whole by something far greater. Where the fey you have lived with your life become warped and disfigured. And as a heart of darkness threatens to swallow you and all you hold dear whole, only for a red-hooded figure atop a Fealgarn Stag to suddenly appear and strike down the Warped Fey. A dozen other mounted warriors charging through and scattering the creatures. The figure gives a smile of reassurance then rides on to save the day and live happily ever after.

Or so the story goes that I told my daughter. All but the end, I can claim validity. Though I never did see that red-hood again, I wish to believe she, the huntsmen, and the huntresses that saved us that day saw a hero’s ending.

Effects: Land Leader Shock: +1; Shock Damage: +15%.

Idea 3: Oberon's Legacy

Oberon Fealgarn. What can I say that hasn’t been said?

Oberon Fealgarn broke the Greentide. Oberon Fealgarn betrayed the eastern clans. Oberon Fealgarn saved his Salla Fealgarn. Oberon Fealgarn used his clanselves as pawns. Oberon Fealgarn was a patriot. Oberon Fealgarn was a tyrant.

Perhaps even these ramblings of an old elf have been uttered as well, but Oberon Fealgarn was all of this and more. Cyranvar would not be without him. Nor would its violent founding be with him. He was the best of us, and the worst. We would do well to learn from both.

Effects: Stability Cost Modifier: -15%.

Idea 1: Aerial Countercharges

The giant hawks of the Mountain Grove… Certainly they and their riders are famous now, but back then? When I first heard of Bricena Myna’s flight my first reaction was to laugh. Who would be bold enough face down a bird twice the size of an elf much less ride it? If there was such an elf, it was certainly not the ceanna renowned for poise and grace. With jeer, I dismissed the story as just another attempt to sprinkle fairie dust in my eyes by my fellow rangers. By the grace of Seelie and resolve of the Unseelie, I remain ever grateful to have been proven wrong.

Despite having faced an orcish charge two dozen a time, me and my fellow rangers found ourselves scattered. I fully admit to the fear that struck me. To having thoughts of fleeing as disaster struck us. But such fears were crushed, just as the orc that nearly took my head was beneath the talon of a great eagle. I never had the chance to thank my rescuer. They had taken off before I could even gain my bearings. Despite that, my comrades never stopped squawking it was Bricena herself who saved me. A jest I will grudgingly tolerate for my life.

Idea 3: Shared Projects

For all of its claims, Elynaile will never hold the same splendor in my eyes as Ciranmyna. No matter what the elves of the Lake Grove say, every elf knows what city shines as the jewel of the forest. And if there had been any room for doubt before Bricena’s reign, those doubts were well dismissed by its end. Drennen druidship, Ayeth architecture, Ahain silver… the city contains the works of each clan in multitudes. The city truly stands as a testament to the shared work of the salla, even before Cyranvar came to be. Even to this day, as I stroll the winding streets, I can spy members of each Great Salla still eagerly working together to build something even greater.

Seelie Queen smile upon her, in all my years, never have I met someone as sweet and dogged as her. Forty years and she still tries to bring the light of the Jadd to my life.

Effects: Domestic Trade Power: +20%.

Idea 6: Ash Children

By the time those feyscorned guns made their way to Cyranvar, my days as a soldier were long behind me. The same could not be said for my wayward daughter. When I look back, I feel pride. Her skill as a sharpshooter easily outclassed my own and her sense of duty toward our people mirrored my own when the forest was still divided between the clans. But at the time, I could only shake my head in disapproval. She and her cohort acted like any sapling would, rebellious and brash. They needed a stern hand to correct this.

To my then bafflement, the Ceannacai encouraged this new generation’s behavior. Dubbing them Ash Children, they were marched to battle equipped with those ructious weapons. Gone were the simple days of the bow and glaive. It was a new era, one filled with bellowing smoke, manic war cries, and neverending cacophony of fire.

Effects: Cavalry Fire: +15%.

Idea 7: The War of the Black Tower

Something said can never be unsaid. And after words not worth repeating, my daughter left my shop. Fury gripped me at first, but when she did not return, anger chilled to sorrow. I could not find her, and so I gave myself to my work. Built a mercantile empire dedicated to tracking my lost scion. I did not care when the War of Treachery began. I paid no heed as Esthil and its Witch-Queen lich rose the dead to fight their perverse war.

Even as the old elven clans who had settled Escann warned of the growing threat, not a word could reach my ears. It was only when a young man carrying a shattered sword showed up to my step was I shaken from stupor. At my first sight, and to my shame, all I saw was the union of an elf… and an orc. It was only when I locked eyes with him did I see him for who he was, not simply what.

He was Elrac of Dustandar, proud member of Arturos’ Watch. And he was my grandson.

I cannot begin to express my regrets here. Nor is there time. Elrac, just as his mother, and perhaps just as this old elf was, is driven by sworn duty. No… I remember my oath well. Evil is ascendent and my kin are in need. I will organize an audience for Elrac with the Ceannacai. Cyranvar and its commander must act.

Effects: Army Tradition: +1; Diplomatic Reputation: +100% (inherited display; percentage conversion unverified).
